title: Likelihood ratio test
dek: Ask whether extra parameters earn their keep by comparing nested maxima of the same likelihood.
story: A likelihood ratio test is not a generic model bake-off. It asks a sharper question: if a simpler model is a restricted version of a fuller one, does the extra freedom move the maximized log-likelihood enough to be implausible under the restriction?

Write the reduced model as a subset of the full parameter space — usually by setting some coordinates to 0, or by tying parameters together. Fit both by maximum likelihood. The evidence against the restriction is twice the gap between those two peaks.

Under regularity, that gap is referred to a χ² distribution whose degrees of freedom equal the number of restrictions. If the gap is large relative to that reference, the reduced model is not an adequate special case of the full one.
deep: Let ℓ(θ) be the log-likelihood. Suppose Θ₀ ⊂ Θ₁, with dim(Θ₁) − dim(Θ₀) = k. The Wilks statistic is Λ = 2(ℓ(θ̂₁) − ℓ(θ̂₀)). Under H₀: θ ∈ Θ₀, and standard regularity (identifiable interior point, interchange of derivative and integral, non-singular information), Λ →d χ²_k.

The same comparison is the difference in residual deviance for GLMs: D₀ − D₁, which is exactly Λ when both models are estimated by ML in an exponential family. Wald and score tests are first-order equivalent to the LRT, but they are not the same finite-sample object: Wald uses only the full-model curvature, score uses only the reduced-model slope.

Regularity fails on the boundary. Testing a variance component at 0, a mixture weight at 0, or a parameter on the edge of the simplex does not give a plain χ². The null distribution becomes a mixture of chi-squares, and p-values computed as χ²_k are anti-conservative. Phylogenetic and random-effect models in TB genomics hit this issue constantly.

Non-nested models (different mean structures that are not restrictions of each other) are outside Wilks. Use Vuong, AIC/BIC as estimates of predictive risk, or an encompassing model — but do not report an LRT p-value.

Wald and score tests are the other two members of the trinity (own plate). AIC and BIC reuse 2Δℓ with a penalty instead of a χ² tail (own plate). They are not LRTs with a different font. If the scientific job is a nested restriction, write Λ and k. If the job is predictive ranking of non-nested mean structures, write AIC and admit you left Wilks.

formulas.label: Wilks statistic
formulas.note: Twice the log-likelihood gap between the unrestricted and restricted maxima.

formulas.label: Reference under H₀
formulas.note: Holds when the true parameter is interior and the information matrix is invertible.

visual.caption: The reduced model is a subset of the full parameter space. Wilks’ statistic is twice the vertical gap between the two maximized log-likelihoods, referred to χ² with degrees of freedom equal to the number of restrictions.

example.title: Lineage as an extra term in a Bernoulli GLM
example.setup: n = 240 RR-TB isolates. Outcome: 1 if phenotypic moxifloxacin MIC > critical concentration. Reduced model: logit π = β₀ + β_fq (presence of a gyrA QRDR mutation). Full model adds lineage (L2 vs other) and the mutation×lineage interaction. Maximized log-likelihoods: ℓ₀ = −98.4 (2 parameters), ℓ₁ = −93.1 (4 parameters).

steps.title: Confirm nesting
steps.body: Setting β_lin = 0 and β_int = 0 inside the full linear predictor recovers the reduced model exactly. The LRT is licensed. If the reduced model used a different link, or dropped the main mutation term while keeping the interaction, nesting would fail.

steps.title: Compute Λ
steps.body: The gap in log-likelihood is −93.1 − (−98.4) = 5.3. Double it.

steps.title: Choose the reference
steps.body: Two extra parameters, both interior (log-odds), so k = 2. Compare 10.6 to χ²_2. The 0.95 quantile of χ²_2 is 5.99; 10.6 sits near the 0.005 tail (p ≈ 0.005).

steps.title: Say what was tested
steps.body: Rejecting H₀ means lineage (and/or its interaction with gyrA) improves the Bernoulli likelihood enough that a two-parameter restriction is implausible. It does not by itself prove a biological interaction — look at the coefficient, the counts per lineage, and possible confounding by treatment history.

example.takeaway: Nesting, twice the log-likelihood gap, χ² with Δp degrees of freedom — and a sentence about the scientific restriction, not just a star.

check.prompt: When is a likelihood ratio test the right comparison between two models?
choices: Whenever AIC is smaller for the fuller model
When the reduced model is a parameter restriction of the fuller model
When both models are linear in the parameters
check.answer: When the reduced model is a parameter restriction of the fuller model
check.why: Wilks’ theorem is a statement about nested parameter spaces. AIC can be computed for non-nested models; linearity and n > 30 are neither necessary nor sufficient.

whyWrong.Whenever AIC is smaller for the fuller m: AIC is a predictive criterion, not a nested-model test, and it can be used when models are not nested.
whyWrong.When both models are linear in the param: LRTs are used constantly in nonlinear and GLM settings. Nesting, not linearity, is the requirement.
whyWrong.When the sample size exceeds 30: The χ² reference is an asymptotic statement. n = 30 does not license comparing non-nested models.

check.prompt: A reduced GLM has maximized log-likelihood −120.4 with 3 parameters. The full model has −116.1 with 5 parameters. What is Λ, and what is the usual H₀ reference?
check.why: Λ = 2(−116.1 − (−120.4)) = 2(4.3) = 8.6. Degrees of freedom are the number of extra parameters, 5 − 3 = 2, not the total parameter count.

whyWrong.Λ = 4.3, referred to χ²_5: You forgot to double the log-likelihood gap, and the df are the difference in dimension, not the full model’s parameter count.
whyWrong.Λ = 8.6, referred to χ²_8: The statistic is right; the df are not a sum of parameter counts.
whyWrong.Λ = 236.5, referred to N(0,1): That is not how a likelihood ratio is formed.

check.prompt: On the nested-model plate, what does the inner region represent?
check.figureHint: Look at the nested boxes labeled reduced and full.
choices: The sampling distribution of the MLE under the alternative
The set of parameter values allowed by the reduced model
The rejection region of the χ² test
The posterior support of a Bayesian model
check.answer: The set of parameter values allowed by the reduced model
check.why: Nesting is a statement about parameter spaces: Θ₀ sits inside Θ₁. The χ² curve is the reference for the scalar statistic Λ, not the inner box itself.

whyWrong.The sampling distribution of the MLE und: That would be a density on the estimate, not a subset of parameter space.
whyWrong.The rejection region of the χ² test: Rejection lives on the Λ axis, to the right of a χ² quantile.
whyWrong.The posterior support of a Bayesian mode: The plate is frequentist geometry. A posterior would need a prior measure.
